# What this system does

> Draft generated by reading the code — **not approved documentation**. Every statement cites the
> file it was read from. Correct what is wrong: the value of this document comes from your
> developers' review, not from the automatic reading.

Harbourline takes freight bookings for a shipping line. It is four repositories:

- `harbourline` — the booking service. A booking is made against a quote (`harbourline/bookings.py`)
  and only when the sailing has room left (`harbourline/capacity.py`).
- `harbourline-pricing` — the freight price: chargeable weight, the lane's rate, the surcharges
  (`pricing/freight.py`, `pricing/surcharges.py`).
- `harbourline-tracking` — what is at sea: the events a sailing emits and its expected arrival
  (`tracking/events.py`, `tracking/eta.py`).
- `harbourline-web` — the shipper's web front end: asks for a quote and books against it
  (`src/quote.ts`, `src/booking.ts`).

## How the parts talk

The web front end calls the pricing service for a quote and the booking service to book. The
tracking service emits `sailing.delayed` when a sailing's expected arrival moves; the booking
service knows who is booked on it.
